strategies.name: support_to_resistance_scalp
strategies.entry_summary: After allowing the first 5 to 15 minutes to establish support on the 5-minute chart, enter long when price comes down into a recognized support area and bounces. The transcript teaches using moving-average support such as the 13 EMA or, if that fails, deeper support such as the 200 EMA, as well as a
strategies.exit_summary: Exit the scalp at resistance or after a quick upward move; the repeated management rule is to get in and out quickly, take profit fast, and not overstay the trade.

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: wait for the first 5 to 15 minutes to pass, then buy the touch/bounce off the 13 EMA acting as support
variants.target_note: sell into the quick move up / resistance
variants.transcript_quote: this 13 EMA operated as a initial support... the stock came down and it hit right there that's our entry for a scalp

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: after the 13 EMA loses support status, buy the bounce from deeper support at the 200 EMA
variants.target_note: ride it to resistance and exit
variants.transcript_quote: another quick Scout this one off a deeper support sitting at the 200 EMA once the 13 EMA gave up its support status

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: identify where price repeatedly bottoms and bounces / demand zones, then enter at that support
variants.transcript_quote: take a quick small trade that you see at support sell right at resistance

consensus.enumeration_note: The video teaches one promoted strategy: a long support-bounce scalp sold into resistance/quick upside. A later short-after-support-break move is mentioned with an entry, but its exit is only gestural ('you want to exit right there'), so under Rule 1 it remains an unpromoted mention, not a second strategy object.
